note:
552 -> 483. The floor it replaces was never the tree's, and the repair is an append, not a re-export.

THE OLD FLOOR DID NOT REPRODUCE. At b1372924dd6, the commit that set 552, the
tree measures 541 -- with that commit's own checker and with HEAD's, which is how
the checker is ruled out as the difference:

    old tree + old checker  541      old tree + HEAD checker  541
    HEAD tree + old checker 561      HEAD tree + HEAD checker 561

So the checker has not moved and the tree drifted 541 -> 561 (+20) under a floor
of 552 that sat between them. Per-module, old tree -> HEAD:

    documents_product 0 -> 14    account   0 -> 10    data_recycle 0 -> 4
    calendar          4 ->  5    crm       0 ->  1    base_vat     0 -> 1
    base_automation  42 -> 43    product  48 -> 42    base         6 -> 0

A RE-EXPORT WOULD HAVE DELETED LIVE STRINGS. The seven modules were installed
into one database and exported; measured against the catalogue on disk, that
export DROPS 171 msgids from account alone -- "Accounts Payable", "Accumulated
Depreciation", "Automatic Tax Mapping (AvaTax)" and the rest of the chart and
localization terms, whose records a seven-module database has never held. Also
21 from crm, 16 from calendar, 10 from base_automation, 6 from data_recycle.
None of them is dead; they are strings whose records that install set cannot
see, and writing the export over the file strands every translation of them.
Only documents_product came out purely additive.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD. For each module, the blocks for exactly the strings the
gate reports unresolved, copied verbatim out of that fresh export so their
`#.`/`#:` references are the exporter's own, appended to a file otherwise left
byte-for-byte alone:

    documents_product +14   account +10   base_automation +40   data_recycle +4
    calendar +4   crm +1   base_vat +1                       = 74 blocks

Verified: every git diff is additions only (-0 on all seven); msgid sets
compared against HEAD show 0 lost in every file; and all seven parse with
odoo.tools.translate.PoFileReader, which is the consumer that matters.

The floor is the tree again. Re-export properly -- from a database whose
install set is at least the one the catalogue was built from -- before trusting
a bulk rewrite of any of these files.
